label: State-space model (S4D with a pointwise encoder)
family_label: State-space and recurrent models (S4D diagonal state space)

compute.eval_note: harness evaluate.py per rung (800 sim val runs + 52 dev basins) not included: about 0.5-4 CPU-min per rung
compute.notes: 4 rungs; one thread (torch.set_num_threads(1)), time.process_time() of the training process, shared 2-core machine

feature_engineering: None beyond the shared arms_seq pipeline (common/seqlib.py), identical for all four sequence arms: FlowCast's 11 scaled daily features (P/10, log1p P, PET/5, T_mean/T_min/T_max /10, SRAD/150, vp/1000, wind/3, sin/cos day of year) + FlowCast's 18-value static vector (batch["static"], standardised with the train bank mean/sd) repeated every day; target in units of the basin mean precipitation exp(static[11]); 730-day windows (365 warm-up + 365 target), inference in 365-day blocks each with its own 365-day warm-up (FlowCast). Causal: day t uses forcing up to day t only.
rule: keep if sim val median NSE (all 800 frozen runs) > incumbent + 0.01 AND dev median NSE (52 dev basins, WY2001-2014) >= 0.95 x incumbent's

rungs.change: base: S4D (3 layers, 48 channels, 16 complex modes each), FlowCast's training recipe (3000 steps)

rungs.why: sim +0.001 (0.399 vs 0.398): unlike the LSTM, TCN and transformer, the linear time-invariant SSM gains nothing from more training (dev 0.428).

rungs.change: pointwise nonlinear encoder before the SSM layers (residual MLP 48 -> 48 -> 48, GELU); 30.4k parameters; 6000 steps
rungs.why: sim 0.422 vs incumbent r0 0.398 (+0.024; r1 shows the 6000 steps alone add nothing) and dev 0.435 >= 0.95 x 0.410: kept. Released (r3 did not beat it). A nonlinearity BEFORE the linear memory (e.g. rain vs snow, thresholds) is what the fixed filter lacked.

rungs.change: Mamba-lite: replace the S4D layers by selective state-space layers (input-dependent step dt and input/output maps B, C; scalar decay per head, 6 heads x 8, state 16; Mamba-2 style, gated output; no pre-MLP); 28.9k parameters; 6000 steps
rungs.why: sim 0.415 vs incumbent r2 0.422 (-0.007; dev 0.429 vs 0.435). Selectivity beats the plain fixed filter (r1 0.399) but not the fixed filter with a nonlinear encoder in front. torch's chunked SSD equals numpy's day-by-day recurrence to 1.6e-15 (float64).

export_check.note: numpy float64 (released predict.py) vs torch float32 (training checkpoint), mm/day, 16 sim val windows + 3 dev basins (14 years each)

bands: raw pinball quantiles (no dev widening; arm C conformalises every arm)
